_meta.title: Family and Friends 4 — Assessment Seed
_meta.note: Question TOPICS and STEMS only — not actual quiz questions. Use this file as input when generating lesson checks.

grammarPatterns: Gerund after opinion verb: I love ___ (swimming / to swim / swims)
Frequency adverb placement: She ___ goes hiking. (always / always she / she always)
How often question form: ___ do you go cycling? (How often / How many / How much)
Negative opinion: He hates ___ up early. (get / getting / got)
sampleStems: Which activity involves taking photos as a hobby?
Choose the correct sentence: 'I love [swim / swimming / swam] in the sea.'
Fill in: 'How ___ do you go cycling?' (often / many / much)
Which adverb means 'not very often, but sometimes'?
True/False: 'enjoy' is followed by the -ing form of a verb
Complete: 'She ___ (never / always) does her homework late — she is very responsible.'

grammarPatterns: Short adjective comparative: London is ___ than Hanoi in winter. (colder / more cold / coldest)
Long adjective comparative: A hurricane is ___ than a thunderstorm. (more dangerous / dangerouser / most dangerous)
Irregular comparative: Yesterday was ___ than today. (badder / worse / more bad)
as...as: Today is ___ cold ___ yesterday. (as / so / more)
sampleStems: What do we call a very long period with almost no rain?
Choose the correct comparative: 'Today is [hotter / more hot / hot] than yesterday.'
True/False: We use 'more' before short one-syllable adjectives like 'cold'.
Fill in: 'A blizzard is ___ than regular snow.' (more dangerous / dangerouser / most dangerous)
What word means 'extremely cold (informal)'?
Complete: 'The heatwave was ___ than last summer.' (bad → ___)

grammarPatterns: Present continuous for now: Look — the train ___! (is leaving / leaves / left)
Present continuous for future: We ___ the 5pm ferry tomorrow. (are taking / take / took)
Question form: ___ you ___ to the airport now? (Are / going / Are...going)
Negative: She ___ cycling to school today — it's raining. (isn't / don't / not)
sampleStems: Which transport travels underwater?
Choose the correct form: 'Look! The children [are running / run / ran] for the bus!'
True/False: We can use present continuous for fixed future plans.
Fill in: 'They ___ flying to London next Monday.' (are / is / do)
What does 'board' mean in the context of travel?
Complete: 'We missed the ferry — the next one ___ at 3pm.' (is leaving / leaves — both may be correct, discuss which to use and why)

grammarPatterns: going to affirmative: She ___ buy a new coat. (is going to / going to / will)
going to question: ___ you going to wear boots today? (Are / Is / Do)
going to negative: I ___ going to spend all my money. (am not / don't / isn't)
going to + base verb: He is going to ___ on those jeans. (try / tries / trying)
sampleStems: What do you call a strip of cloth worn around the neck for warmth?
Choose the correct form: 'I [am going to / going to / will going to] buy some gloves.'
True/False: After 'going to', we use the past form of the verb.
Fill in: '___ she going to try on those boots?' (Is / Are / Does)
What does 'in stock' mean?
Complete: 'I can't afford this coat — it's too ___.' (expensive / discount / receipt)

grammarPatterns: Uncountable noun with some: We need ___ flour for the cake. (some / any / a)
any in question: Is there ___ milk in the fridge? (any / some / a)
How much vs how many: ___ eggs do we need? (How many / How much / How often)
Uncountable — no plural: I bought three ___. (rices ❌ / rice ✅)
sampleStems: Which food is uncountable — you cannot say 'two ___'?
Choose: 'Is there [some / any] sugar in the cupboard?'
True/False: 'Rice' is a countable noun — we can say 'three rices'.
Fill in: 'How ___ butter do we need?' (much / many / often)
What cooking method uses steam from boiling water?
Complete: 'We don't have ___ cheese — we need to buy some.' (any / some / a)

grammarPatterns: Irregular past: We ___ to the market yesterday. (went / go / goed)
Past negative: She ___ eat breakfast this morning. (didn't / doesn't / don't)
Past question: ___ you see that film last week? (Did / Do / Does)
Regular past: He ___ his homework an hour ago. (finished / finish / finishes)
sampleStems: What is the past simple form of 'buy'?
Choose the correct sentence: 'She [went / goed / go] to the zoo last Sunday.'
True/False: In past simple questions, we use 'did' + past form of the verb.
Fill in: '___ you eat breakfast this morning? — Yes, I ___.' (Did / did)
What does 'the day before yesterday' mean?
Complete: 'They didn't ___ swimming — they played tennis.' (go / went / going)

grammarPatterns: should for advice: You ___ rest and drink water. (should / must / have to)
shouldn't for negative advice: She ___ eat spicy food with a stomachache. (shouldn't / mustn't / didn't)
should question: ___ I see a doctor? (Should / Must / Do)
should + base verb: You should ___ to bed early. (go / going / went)
sampleStems: What is the joint between your hand and your arm called?
Choose: 'You [should / shouldn't] eat lots of vegetables — they are good for you.'
True/False: We say 'You should to rest' when giving health advice.
Fill in: '___ I put a plaster on this cut?' (Should / Must / Do)
What is a 'bruise'?
Complete: 'She has a blister on her heel. She ___ wear more comfortable shoes.' (should / shouldn't — choose the right one)

grammarPatterns: can for ability: A dolphin ___ swim very fast. (can / could / cans)
can't for inability: Fish ___ breathe air. (can't / couldn't / don't can)
could for past ability: She ___ ride a bike when she was five. (could / can / cans)
couldn't for past inability: I ___ speak English before I started school. (couldn't / can't / didn't could)
sampleStems: What do we call a huge slow-moving river of ice?
Choose: 'My brother [can / could / cans] play chess when he was four years old.'
True/False: 'Could' is used for past ability, while 'can' is used for present ability.
Fill in: 'Before taking lessons, I ___ swim at all.' (couldn't / can't / didn't)
What is 'deforestation'?
Complete: 'Glaciers ___ melt if we don't reduce global warming.' (can / could — present possibility)
